  The City of San Marino appreciates your attendance. Citizens’ interest provides the Council with
  valuable information regarding issues of the community.

  Regular meetings are held on the 2nd Wednesday of every month at 6:00 p.m. Typically, adjourned

  In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who requires

  PURSUANT TO EXECUTIVE ORDER N-29-20

  CORONAVIRUS DISEASE (COVID-19) ADVISORY
  As a precaution to protect both staff, our constituents, and elected officials, the City is asking
  members of the public to follow the State Health Department’s guidance on mask wearing if
  attending this meeting. Given the seriousness of COVID-19, you are encouraged to
  watch or listen to the meeting from home, or provide input electronically, if you do
  not feel comfortable attending in person.

  Members of the public may observe and offer comment at this meeting telephonically or
  otherwise electronically:

  during the meeting, prior to the close of public comment on an item, to be read by the
  City Clerk during public comment. Lengthy public comment may be summarized in the

  NEW BUSINESS

  1. CONSIDERATION OF CITY CLUB REQUEST TO WAIVE THE LACY PARK
  PERMIT FEE FOR THE INDEPENDENCE DAY VIP PAVILION

  Recommendation: The City Club has requested the City Council waive the group activity fee for
  Lacy Park for the City Club’s 2021 VIP Pavilion.

  ADJOURNMENT

  Dated: June 22, 2021  CHRISTINA BAKER
  Posted: June 22, 2021  CITY CLERK

Page 2 of 4
   Ken Ude, Mayor
  Susan Jakubowski, Vice Mayor
  Steven W. Huang, DDS, Council Member
  Gretchen Shepherd Romey, Council Member
  Steve Talt, Council Member

  TO:  Mayor and City Council
  FROM:  Marcella Marlowe, Ph.D., City Manager

  DATE:  June 25, 2021
  SUBJECT:  CONSIDERATION OF CITY CLUB REQUEST TO WAIVE THE
  LACY PARK PERMIT FEE FOR THE INDEPENDENCE DAY VIP
  PAVILION

  STRATEGIC PLAN CRITICAL SUCCESS FACTORS

  • Engaged and Connected Residents
  • Efficient, Responsive, and Effective City Services
  • Fiscally Responsible and Transparent City Government

  BACKGROUND

  Historically, the City of San Marino hosts a grand Independence Day event annually on July 4th
  of every given year. The day kicks off with the Blecksmith 5K Run, then continues with the
  Independence Day Parade, and concludes with a program of events and fireworks at a full-to-
  capacity Lacy Park fireworks show. (Please note that neither the run, nor the parade, is
  sponsored by the City.) The event is the centerpiece of our community engagement efforts
  throughout the year.

  In 2020, the event was cancelled due to COVID-19. On April 30, 2021, the City Council
  decided, on a split 3/2 vote, to again not hold the event in 2021 largely as a result of the health
  protocols in place at the time and the challenge for staff in having only two months to plan for
  an event that typically takes six months. On June 9, 2021, as a result of the changed health
  protocols, the City Council unanimously directed staff to host the Independence Day
  celebration, to be as similar as possible to our “normal” event.

  Upon inquiry, Rotary declined to run the parade, but City Club was excited about hosting its
  “VIP Pavilion.” As planning has begun in earnest, City Club is requesting consideration from the
  City regarding the required activity fee to use Lacy Park.

Page 3 of 4  1-1
   DISCUSSION

  City Club President Kelly Ryan has requested that the City waive the $145 Lacy Park fee. The
  fee was paid to the City on June 22, 2021. The San Marino Municipal Code does not give the
  City Manager the authority to waive fees of any amount. As a result, Council deliberation and
  action are required. If the Council agrees to waive the fee, the City will return the $145 check
  to City Club.

  FISCAL IMPACT & PROCUREMENT REVIEW

  If the City waives the $145 activity fee for Lacy Park, that will be lost revenue.

  Procurement review is not applicable.

  LEGAL REVIEW

  The City Attorney has reviewed and approved this report as to form.

  RECOMMENDATION

  City Club has requested that the City waive the $145 Lacy Park activity fee. If the City Council
  concurs with City Club’s request, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to waive the group activity fee for Lacy Park for the City Club’s 2021 VIP Pavilion.”

  ATTACHMENTS

  None.
